knowledge:
- key_parameters: targetsfile=Path to the BED file containing target regions ;; readsfile=Path to the BED or BAM file containing aligned reads ;; zerobased=Logical indicating if input coordinates are 0-based (set to FALSE if coordinates are already 1-based) ;; filetype=Set to "bam" in get.reads to read BAM files directly ;; Offset=Bases to enlarge targets on each side to capture near-target reads ;; perBase=Logical in coverage.target to return base-level coverage ;; perTarget=Logical in coverage.target to return target-level coverage ;; destDir=Output directory for HTML reports
- alternatives: BAM files over BED files=Reading BAM files using get.reads(filetype="bam") is much faster because it utilizes ShortRead's scanBam ;; multiTEQCreport=Use to aggregate multiple single-sample TEQC reports instead of manually inspecting individual reports one-by-one
- when_to_use: Appropriate for target capture (enrichment) experiments (such as exome sequencing or custom hybridization panels) to evaluate capture specificity, enrichment, coverage depth, coverage uniformity, and PCR duplication rates.
- pitfalls: Do not use read pairs from reads2pairs for coverage calculations in coverage.target as it spans the entire insert size where there is no actual sequence coverage, leading to inflated coverage estimates ;; Coordinate shifting defaults to 1-based conversion, so if input coordinates are already 1-based, zerobased must be set to FALSE to prevent incorrect shifting ;; Removing duplicates in single-end data can dramatically decrease coverage compared to paired-end data where pair-end coordinate matching preserves more unique reads.

workflows.name: automated_html_reports
workflows.intent: Generate automated single-sample and multi-sample HTML quality control reports.
input: ExampleSet_Reads.bed (aligned reads BED or BAM file)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the TEQC library ;; 2. Define paths to target and read files ;; 3. Run TEQCreport to generate a single-sample HTML report ;; 4. Run multiTEQCreport to combine multiple single-sample reports into a summary report.
workflows.code:
library(TEQC)
exptPath <- system.file("extdata", package = "TEQC")
readsfile <- file.path(exptPath, "ExampleSet_Reads.bed")
targetsfile <- file.path(exptPath, "ExampleSet_Targets.bed")
TEQCreport(sampleName = "Test Sample", targetsName = "Human Exome", referenceName = "Human Genome", destDir = "report", reads = get.reads(readsfile, skip = 0, idcol = 4), targets = get.targets(targetsfile, skip = 0), genome = "hg19")
multiTEQCreport(singleReportDirs = c("report", "report2"), samplenames = c("Sample A","Sample B"), projectName = "Test Project", targetsName = "Human Exome", referenceName = "Human Genome", destDir = "multiTEQCreport")

workflows.name: custom_qc_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform a step-by-step programmatic quality control analysis of target capture data including specificity, coverage, duplicates, and reproducibility.
input: ExampleSet_Reads.bed (aligned reads BED or BAM file)
workflows.stages: 1. Load targets and reads data ;; 2. Convert reads to pairs for paired-end data and plot insert sizes ;; 3. Calculate specificity, enrichment, and plot chromosome distribution ;; 4. Calculate coverage statistics and plot coverage distribution, uniformity, and GC bias ;; 5. Analyze and plot read duplicates ;; 6. Assess reproducibility across samples.
workflows.code:
library(TEQC)
exptPath <- system.file("extdata", package = "TEQC")
targets <- get.targets(targetsfile=paste(exptPath, "ExampleSet_Targets.bed", sep="/"), chrcol = 1, startcol = 2, endcol = 3, skip = 0)
ft <- fraction.target(targets, genome = "hg38")
reads <- get.reads(paste(exptPath, "ExampleSet_Reads.bed", sep="/"), chrcol = 1, startcol = 2, endcol = 3, idcol = 4, zerobased = F, skip = 0)
readpairs <- reads2pairs(reads)
insert.size.hist(readpairs, breaks=10)
chrom.barplot(reads, targets)
fr <- fraction.reads.target(reads, targets)
fraction.reads.target(reads, targets, Offset=100)
fr / ft
fraction.reads.target(readpairs, targets)
Coverage <- coverage.target(reads, targets, perTarget=T, perBase=T)
targets2 <- Coverage$targetCoverages
targets2 <- readsPerTarget(reads, targets2)
covered.k(Coverage$coverageTarget, k=c(1, 5, 10))
coverage.hist(Coverage$coverageTarget, covthreshold=8)
coverage.uniformity(Coverage)
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
coverage.targetlength.plot(targets2, plotcolumn="nReads", pch=16, cex=1.5)
coverage.targetlength.plot(targets2, plotcolumn="avgCoverage", pch=16, cex=1.5)
baitsfile <- paste(exptPath, "ExampleSet_Baits.txt", sep="/")
baits <- get.baits(baitsfile, chrcol=3, startcol=4, endcol=5, seqcol=2)
coverage.GC(Coverage$coverageAll, baits, pch=16, cex=1.5)
coverage.plot(Coverage$coverageAll, targets, Offset=100, chr="chr1", Start=11157524, End=11158764)
duplicates.barplot(reads, targets)
duplicates.barplot(readpairs, targets, ylab="Fraction of read pairs")
reads.collapsed <- unique(reads)
ID.nondups <- names(unique(readpairs))
reads.collapsed.pairs <- reads[names(reads) %in% ID.nondups,,drop=T]
coverage.target(reads.collapsed, targets, perBase=F, perTarget=F)
coverage.target(reads.collapsed.pairs, targets, perBase=F, perTarget=F)
r <- sample(length(reads), 0.1 * length(reads))
reads2 <- reads[-r,,drop=T]
Coverage2 <- coverage.target(reads2, targets, perBase=T)
covlist <- list(Coverage, Coverage2)
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
coverage.density(covlist)
coverage.density(covlist, normalized=F)
coverage.uniformity(Coverage, addlines=F)
coverage.uniformity(Coverage2, addlines=F, add=T, col="blue", lty=2)
coverage.plot(Coverage$coverageAll, targets, Offset=100, chr="chr1", Start=11157524, End=11158764)
coverage.plot(Coverage2$coverageAll, add=T, col.line=2, chr="chr1", Start=11157524, End=11158764)
coverage.correlation(covlist, plotfrac=0.1, cex.pch=4)
